[[File: Colours of Kilkenny.svg|border|20px]] [[Henry Shefflin]] (1–24) |previous=[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1998|1998]] |next=[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2000|2000]] }} The '''1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 113th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The draw for the provincial fixtures took place on 15 November 1998. The championship ran from 22 May to 12 September 1999. [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] entered the championship as the [[1998 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]], however, they were beaten by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[#All-Ireland semi-finals|All-Ireland semi-final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/offalys-reign-ends-as-cork-novices-ride-luck-in-thriller/26140687.html|title=Offaly's reign ends as Cork novices ride luck in thriller|publisher=Irish Independent|date=9 August 1999|access-date=29 June 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40803822.html|title=Cork hurlers renew rivalry with underdogs Offaly|publisher=Echo Live|date=11 February 2022|access-date=29 June 2025}} [[Meath GAA|Meath]], who had participated in the championship since 1993, declined to field a team. The [[#All-Ireland final|All-Ireland final]] was played on 12 September 1999 at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]], between Cork and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], in what was their 21st championship meeting overall and their first All-Ireland final-meeting in [[1992 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland final|seven years]]. Cork won the match by 0–13 to 0–12 to claim their 28th championship title overall and a first tile in [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|nine years]].{{cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40895819.html|title=Echo 130: Seven of the greatest Cork hurling wins as seen through the eyes of The Echo|publisher=Echo Live|date=15 June 2022|access-date=29 June 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/championship-flashback-all-ireland-shc-final-september-1999/26466919.html|title=Championship Flashback: All-Ireland SHC final, September 1999|publisher=Irish Independent|date=4 August 2008|access-date=29 June 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2006/0902/208641-cork/|title=Cork v Kilkenny Classics – 1999 SHC final|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=14 June 2007|access-date=29 June 2025}} Cork's [[Joe Deane]] and Kilkenny's [[Henry Shefflin]] were the championship's top scorers with 1–24 apiece. Cork's [[Brian Corcoran]] was the choice for Hurler of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40128020.html|title=The Leeside legends series: Corcoran was a majestic hurler in every position|publisher=Echo Live|date=23 April 2020|access-date=29 June 2025}} == Team changes == === To Championship === Promoted from the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship]] * None
